Hi Suzanne —

Thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Vivek (deploy/runtime) and Mina (security/compliance). High-level answers up front:

1) EU-only residency: supported via Private deployment with region-scoped VPCs, customer-managed routing, and optional data-plane encryption keys in a customer KMS. We can ensure all inference traffic and persistent KV caches originate and terminate within EU subnets.

2) APAC primary / EU warm-standby: supported as a warm-standby topology with asynchronous state replication. Warm standby is possible but requires explicit replication configuration and acceptance of RPO tradeoffs (minutes).

3) Active-active with jurisdictional routing: technically feasible but requires careful legal sign-off and explicit routing policies — we cannot automatically split single-tenant PII across jurisdictions without documented consent.

Vivek, can you attach a sample network diagram and the routing options matrix? Mina — can you list the evidence package Acme should expect for Legal review (logs, KMS separation proof, audit trail, SOC references)?

I propose a short call Tues/Thurs (your timezone) to finalize the SOW items and delivery cadence. We aim to get the SOW to procurement by 30 Jun.

Hi all —

Attaching a trimmed network diagram and a short matrix of the three topologies (attached as redwood-private-deploy-options.md and acme-network-diagram.png). Key technical notes:

- EU-only: Provision customer VPCs in the EU region, deploy inference clusters pinned to EU GPUs, and use private peering (no public egress). We recommend customer-managed KMS in EU for key separation.

- APAC primary / EU warm standby: Use asynchronous snapshot-based replication of model artifacts and a local KV-caching layer. Keep inference traffic local to APAC region; failover plan will require updating DNS + a cold-start window for large models (we estimate 2-6 minutes depending on model size and cache priming).

- Active-active jurisdictional routing: Requires per-tenant routing policies at the load-balancer level. This is operationally heavier (synchronized metrics, cross-region tracing) and increases cost. Only recommend if Legal confirms cross-border replica consistency is allowed.

Network considerations:
- Cross-region traffic should traverse a controlled peering link with enforced ACLs and strict egress rules.
- Replication traffic should be encrypted with TLS1.3 and mutually authenticated mTLS.
- For APAC customers requiring physical data residency, recommend standing up an APAC Private deployment rather than relying on cross-border replication.

Action items (technical):

- [Karthik] Validate routing policy templates + HubSpot entry for SOW routing clauses.

Hi Suzanne & team —

Thanks — a few compliance constraints and the evidence bundle Acme Legal will want: 

1) Key separation: if you require KMS keys per-region, provide key ARNs and we'll show configuration that binds keys to EU hosts only. We support CMKs in customer-managed KMS/HSM.

2) Audit logs: delivery of control-plane and data-plane access logs (token-level request metadata, IPs, timestamps). We can provide log exports to your SIEM endpoint in EU.

3) Access controls: RBAC audit showing which Redwood operators (if any) have escalation access; default is no operator access unless you enable support-JIT.

4) Replication policy proof: clustering config + proof that replicas are only seeded from approved sources (signed manifests).

5) SOC2 / penetration test evidence: we can share SOC2 type II summary and the last pen-test report under NDA.

Caveat on active-active: From a compliance standpoint, if there's a risk of data transiting from EU to APAC for processing, Legal will almost always require documented consent and explicit logging; difficult to meet for patient-level PII without patient consent or a local processing carve-out.

If you want, we can produce a short "Evidence Pack" document with the minimum artifacts Acme Legal will request. I can own that deliverable — ETA: 3 business days once we confirm the required scope.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Suzanne — thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Summary / decisions for SOW DL-9382: 

- Chosen topology: APAC primary with EU warm-standby (Customer preference + latency). We will not pursue active-active at this time.
- Data residency guarantees: Production inference and caches will be pinned to APAC. Replica artifacts stored in EU warm-standby will be encrypted at rest with customer-managed CMKs located in EU. Cross-region replication will be asynchronous and logged.
- Failover behavior: Manual failover initiated by Acme (we will provide a runbook + support-JIT). Estimated failover RTO: 3-6 minutes for model priming + traffic cutover.
- Evidence pack: Mina to deliver the Evidence Pack (KMS config snippets, log export templates, SOC2 summary) by 2027-07-05.
- SOW items: include the network diagram (attached), routing policy clause, and a clause that Acme must approve any active-active attempt. Procurement target: 2027-07-07 to get countersigned.

Next steps / owners:
- [Mina] Evidence Pack by 2027-07-05.

- [Karthik] Add routing clause + HubSpot note (HS-4321) to SOW draft.

If that aligns, I'll move the SOW to procurement and attach the Evidence Pack when available. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if Daniel wants to review the technical proof with Mina/Vivek.
